Subject: Observability partner certification: connector dependency matrix & co-sell playbook

Hi Ruchi / Ben,

Thanks again for the product demos last week. We want to align on the technical dependencies and the certification steps so we can list the Redwood connector in the Grafana and Datadog marketplaces and kick off the co-sell playbook.

Attached is a first-pass dependency matrix (Grafana-Connector-Dependency-Matrix-v1.2.xlsx) and a draft mutual action plan with timeline placeholders. The ask for this thread is to:
- Confirm any missing technical dependencies (agent versions, exporter compatibility, auth flows)
- Surface required security evidence or questionnaires we should prep (SOC2, pen test, dataflow diagrams)
- Agree on milestones for certification + marketplace listing (target: end of Q1 2027)

Internal folks: Ben / Connor / Vanessa—please track any gating items (security artifacts, integration test cases, PS support for early adopters).

Ruchi: can you confirm whether Grafana will accept an OTLP-based exporter or if we need to bundle a Unified Agent integration?
Ben: can you confirm Datadog’s preferred tagging/metric mapping for our metrics pipeline?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Observability partner certification: connector dependency matrix & co-sell playbook

Laura — thanks for the clear packet and timeline. Quick notes after reviewing the matrix:

- Grafana Marketplace accepts connectors via the Connector SDK (preferred) or as a packaged plugin. For metrics ingestion we prefer OTLP/gRPC or the Unified Agent (Grafana Agent) depending on customer environment.
- We call out the following as hard requirements for certification: stable billing doc, clear dataflow diagram, a compatibility matrix (agent versions, kernel constraints), and an e2e test harness that can be run in our CI.
- For OTLP exporters: if you expose a standard OTLP endpoint with protobuf over gRPC and include stable resource attributes, we can onboard it without bundling the Agent. If you need tight out-of-the-box UX (auto-discovery/config), the Agent integration will make certification smoother but adds maintenance.

I'll ask our partner engineering team to validate your attached dependency matrix and map to our SDK checklist. Expect a follow-up with line-by-line comments by 2026-10-14.

Best,
Ruchi
Ruchi Patel | Partner Engineering, Grafana Labs

Hi all — quick note from the Datadog side. We reviewed the matrix and have two technical asks:

1) Tag mapping: please confirm how you intend to surface source, environment, and model_id as standardized tags. Datadog uses env/service/source as minimal required attributes for dashboards and billing correlation.
2) Metric cardinality: we need a plan to limit high-cardinality labels (model_id) for large customers. A recommended approach is sample-based aggregation and optional sampling flags per customer.

We can provide a sample agent exporter and a mapping template you can adopt. If you’d like, we can also run a short lab where we push 100k synthetic events to validate cardinality controls.

Ben Davis
Technical Partnerships, Datadog

If we hit these milestones, we’ll be in a good position to start a private beta with two joint customers in Nov and aim for certification paperwork in Jan.

I’ll update the mutual-action-plan doc with the deadlines and share links once updated.

Regards,
Laura
